Dear Customer,

Thank you for contacting TOPENS. This is Joyce from TOPENS Customer Service Team. It will be a pleasure to assist you today.

I apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused, but do not worry, we will do our best to help you.

Checked with our engineer, please help us do some tests to find out the problem, so that we can provide corresponding help.

1. Please measure the voltage of the +BAT- terminals (11# and 12#) on the control board to see whether it is above 22VDC. If so, please continue to step 2. If not, please check your power source: if you are using an AC adapter, check whether its output voltage is 36VDC. Disconnect the batteries from the control board and measure the battery voltage to see if it is above 22VDC. If the battery voltage is below 22VDC, please fully charge the batteries with an additional charger and connect them to +BAT- (11# and 12#) on the control board, then press the remote to see if it works. If you have a solar system with a TCS3 controller, disconnect the solar panels from the TCS3, disconnect the TCS3 from the control board, and test the battery and TCS3 LOAD terminal voltage. If batteries are over 22VDC but the TCS3 LOAD is under 22VDC, the TCS3 might be defective.

2. Disconnect all accessories from the control board first (just leave the power source and the arm). Disable the photocell function by turning dip switch #3 off. Then erase all remote codes from the control board and reprogram them to have a try. If it fails, please instantaneously short (plug the wire in, then pull it out immediately) the push button terminals (4# and 5#) to check whether the opener can work. You can refer to this video on how to instantaneously short the terminals: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VdDhyHZxmpQE5pG7BYHOJi5GYb7iZHFS/view?usp=sharing

3. If there is still no luck, please release the clutches on the arm and push the gate to the middle position. Engage the clutches and press the remote to see whether the gate can run towards both directions.

4. Please check the motor. Connect the red & black wires of the arm to a DC 24V power source directly; the motor should run. Then exchange the polarity of the wires; the motor should run in the opposite direction. If the motor runs in both directions, the motor itself is good.

5. Disconnect the BLUE, GREEN & YELLOW wires of the arm from the control board, use two jumper wires to short the ULT, COM & DLT terminals to which the wires were connected, and then press the remote to see whether the opener can work.

Please let me know the result one by one.

Videos showing the problem and pictures of the whole control board are much appreciated for further judgement. You can directly send the video to my E-mail via the attachment. If the sending is not successful, please share the photo or video link through dropbox, icloud or google drive. Thanks for your understanding and cooperation.

And also please reply with your specific SHIPPING ADDRESS with zip code and confirm your PHONE # available for further assistance. All TOPENS products are backed by a 12-month warranty.

Thank you again for being a valued customer! Your complete satisfaction is what we strive for. We at TOPENS are always standing by and ready to help.

Best regards,
Joyce
TOPENS Customer Service Team

Dear Customer,

Thank you for contacting TOPENS. This is Joyce from TOPENS Customer Service Team. It will be a pleasure to assist you today.

I apologize for the trouble you're experiencing with the gate opener after just four days. Do not worry, we will do our best to help you. All TOPENS products are backed by a 12-month warranty.

Checked with our engineer, please help us do some tests to find out the problem, so that we can provide corresponding help.

1. Since the lock still unlocks, the motor seems to be running. Please first disengage the clutch and manually push the moving-rod to the middle position. Then, press the remote control to test whether the arm moves.

2. If the arm still does not move, re-engage the clutch and detach the arm from the gate. While pushing the moving-rod inward, rotate the front mount clockwise. If the arm begins to move, the screw nut may have disengaged from the screw rod at the far end. Once the arm is back in the middle position, use the remote control to test operation again. For more guidance, please refer to this article: https://topens.com/blogs/blog-posts/how-to-retract-the-moving-rod-when-the-opener-arm-extends-too-much

3. If the arm is partially extended or fully retracted and still does not move, ensure the clutch is fully and correctly engaged. If engagement looks normal, disassemble the opener arm to check whether clutch components (Part B and Part C) are properly aligned. Also inspect the moving-rod’s screw nut for signs of damage or excessive wear, and verify the connection between the screw rod and the clutch component with bearing (Part C).

4. If abnormal or excessive noise is present from the motor area, the issue may be inside the motor’s reduction gearbox. In this case, please dismantle the gearbox and check the gears inside for damage or slippage.

Please let me know the result one by one. Also, please share some videos showing the control board and the arm's behavior when you press the remote, which will help us judge further. If needed, kindly provide your shipping address with zip code and phone number so we can assist you promptly.

You may find additional help here: https://topens.com/blogs/blog-posts/troubleshooting-guide-motor-operates-but-gate-opener-arm-fails-to-move

Dear Nick,

Thank you for contacting TOPENS. This is Joyce from TOPENS Customer Service Team. It will be a pleasure to assist you today.

It sounds like quite a practical setup, with each household having its own gate but sharing the driveway. I will be happy to clarify the differences between those models and how the control accessories can be configured for your two separate gates.

At TOPENS, all of our products come with a 12-month warranty. More importantly, we provide lifetime technical support via email.

From the picture and your description, your lightweight 3m aluminium gates are well suited for our electromechanical ram-style openers. Before I break down the models, let me address your accessory questions directly, as this will guide our recommendation.

Regarding the accessories and your two-gate setup:
For two independent gates side-by-side, you would need two completely separate single-gate opener kits, not one dual kit, because each gate is operated by a different household. You control each system independently. A single dual opener kit is designed to operate two gate leaves in sync for one wide driveway.
- M12 Remotes: A single remote button can be programmed to open both gates simultaneously, but this is not ideal for your situation where each gate is for a separate household. The standard practice is to program your remote to open only your gate, and the neighbor's remote to open only their gate. You can purchase additional remote controls separately.
- TC196 WiFi Remote: This connects to one control board. You would need one TC196 for your gate opener, and your neighbor would need a separate one for theirs. You then operate your gate through the TOPENS APP on your phone without interfering with each other.
- TC175P Keypad and TC148 Push Button: These are wired directly to one specific control board. You would install one keypad and one push button for your gate, and these would only open your gate. Your neighbor would install their own set for their gate.

Now, to choose the correct models from your list:
- The AT1202 and AT602 are electromechanical ram openers, which are perfect for your pull-to-open, lightweight aluminium gates.
- The KD902 (I believe you meant KD902, not KD702) and A8132 are articulated arm openers, which are typically used for heavier gates swinging on pillared posts and are more power-hungry (24V). They are over-specified for your 20-30kg gates.
- Between the AT1202 and AT602, they are fundamentally the same reliable motor. The difference is in the accessories included. The AT1202 is a "Deluxe" kit that includes a pair of photocells (safety beams) and a wired push button in the box, whereas the AT602 is the standard kit. For the UK, I strongly recommend getting a kit with photocells for safety compliance.

Our Recommendation:
Based on your technical requirements and location, I recommend purchasing **two AT1202 single swing gate opener kits**. One kit will operate your gate, and the other will operate your neighbor's gate completely independently. Your gates are very light, so these will operate them with ease.

Purchasing link on Amazon UK: https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B07H33917Z
User manual for AT1202: https://www.topens.com/upload/2021/03/AT1202-user-manual.pdf
Installation video: https://youtu.be/YA3T3g0sK8Q

I hope this helps clear things up. Please share your order information with me when you purchase the TOPENS gate openers, so I can help you register the warranties. Feel free to contact us if you have any questions or concerns during the product installation and use in the future.

Thank you once again for being a valued customer! Your complete satisfaction is what we strive for. We at TOPENS are always standing by and ready to help.

Best regards,
Joyce
TOPENS Customer Service Team

results.generated_reply_en:
Dear Customer,

Thank you for contacting TOPENS. This is Joyce from TOPENS Customer Service Team. It will be a pleasure to assist you today.

I appreciate your interest in our gate opener accessories. I understand you would like to know the differences between the A8132, PW802, AD8, and AT1202 models. I am happy to clarify this for you.

At TOPENS, all of our products are backed by a 12-month warranty. More importantly, we provide lifetime technical support via email.

These models are different accessories designed for specific purposes:

1. The A8132 and PW802 are push-button remote controls. The A8132 remote is typically compatible with our classic series gate openers (such as the A, AT, and AD series), while the PW802 remote is designed for our newer, modern-style series (such as the DPS, EKPK, and PW series). Their frequency and coding may differ, so they are not interchangeable between the two product lines.

2. The AD8 is an external receiver that can be added to a gate opener control board. It provides extended range or adds compatibility with a specific type of remote control for openers that do not have it built-in.

3. The AT1202 is a transformer used to convert household AC power (usually 110V-120V) to the low-voltage DC power (often 24V) required to run a gate opener control board and charge the backup battery. It is for continuous power supply for an AC-powered system.

To give you the most accurate recommendation, could you please tell me which model of TOPENS gate opener you are using, or provide a photo of the control board? This will help me confirm the exact compatible remote control or accessories for your specific unit.

Hope this can help you. Please feel free to contact us if you have any questions or concerns during the product installation and use in the future.
